 Judgment

The above appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the Judgment and Award dated 08.02.2011 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Holenarasipur, in MVC No.25/2010, by which, the claim petition was dismissed.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
NC: 2023:KHC:20629

When the claimant was walking on Hassan-Mysore road near Bridge of Hemavathi Right Bank channel, with one B.P.Purushotham, on 21.10.2009 at 8.00 a.m., towards Holenarasipur, a TVS motor bike bearing Registration No.KA- 13/L-7480 ridden in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction came in the opposite direction and dashed the claimants.
The claimant in this appeal was studying in 4th standard at the time of the accident.
He sustained severe injuries and was admitted to hospital at Holenarasipur.

Both the claimants filed separate claim petitions and upon consideration of the material on record and evidence adduced, the Sri Dharamaraja vs T R Nanjunde Gowda on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179574048/

sentences.text: 2 Claims Tribunal dismissed both the claim petitions.
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed by the claimant in MVC No.25/2010.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant-claimant submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error on the ground that the claimant had fallen from the bike and thus, the manner in which the accident had occurred was stated in the complaint and the accident is not proved.

Therefore, it is submitted NC: 2023:KHC:20629 that the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition without properly appreciating the evidence on record and prays for setting aside the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal and for granting compensation.
5. Learned counsel for respondent submitted that the Tribunal is justified in dismissing the claim petition upon appreciation of evidence on record correctly.
Therefore, prayed to dismiss the appeal.
In the claim petition, it is narrated that in the accident spot where the claimants were walking, the motor bike had dashed against them and the claimants sustained injuries.
The accident was caused on 21.10.2009 at 8.00 a.m., towards Holenarasipura while they were walking on the bridge.

After the accident, immediately the claimants were shifted to the Government General Hospital,
Holenarasipura, in which the doctor/hospital authorities have recorded information of history of accident as "fall from the bike and sustained injuries."

Accordingly, the same has been registered in the said MLC register extract as per Exs.R1 to R3 that the claimants have fallen from the bike NC:
2023:KHC:20629 and sustained injuries.
But it was striked out and written as "RTA".
Complaint was lodged on the same day at 2.00 p.m., by mentioning that the claimants were walking on the road and a motor bike dashed them and they sustained injuries.
But the information given to the hospital authorities soon after the accident and whatever information given at that undisputed point of time carries more weight.
Another claimant, viz., B.B.Purushothem in MVC No.24/2010 has given information to the hospital authorities.
Further, the said claimant-PW.1 stated that what information he gave was noted down by the doctor/hospital authorities in the MLC register extract.

Therefore, while considering the over- writing, on the said vital aspect, information given that "fall from bike" and later striking it and over-writing as "RTA", creates suspicion regarding the manner of accident as stated in the claim petition.
PW.1-Purushotham has admitted that according to information given to the hospital, the same is written.

Therefore, striking out the word "fall from bike" from the MLC register extract and over-writing as "RTA" is found to be a deliberate act which is to make a claim against the NC: 2023:KHC:20629 Insurance Company.
Therefore, the Tribunal in this regard has correctly appreciated the evidence on record and the findings and reasonings given by the Tribunal are not found to be suffering from any infirmities.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in dismissing the claim petition.

6. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is dismissed.
ii.
The impugned judgment and award dated 08.02.2011 in MVC No.25/2010 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Holenarasipur, is hereby confirmed.
iii. No order as to costs.
